# Overview

Three SmBiT-P2A constructs placed in the MDA-MB-231 CDS landscape, assembled from
the `smBit n`, `p2a`, `HA`, `flag3x` and `egfp` rows of
`accessories/cds seq.xlsx`:

- **SmBiT-P2A-HA**, 120 nt
- **SmBiT-P2A-FLAG**, 117 nt (1x FLAG = the `DYKDDDDK` repeat of `flag3x`)
- **SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP**, 876 nt (the 36 nt Waldo linker sits between the
  FLAG tag and eGFP)

**MDA-MB-231 only**, same background and gene set as `01_`, `03_` and `04_`, so
the panels are directly comparable. Section 5 draws each panel three times: the
HA construct alone, HA + FLAG, and all three.

**NanoLuc is deliberately absent from every panel**, as in `03_` and `04_`.
Section 5 asserts that absence rather than relying on it having been left out.

**Adding eGFP is what moves this family onto the distribution.** The two bare-tag
constructs are ~120 nt, below the 1st percentile of the expressed transcriptome;
they are not points inside the distribution and their reference lines sit on the
y axis, which is why the length panel is also drawn zoomed to 2 kb. FLAG-link-eGFP
at 876 nt is the first construct here that lands inside the gene curves. The
percentiles in section 6 are the numbers to quote for the short pair.

**eGFP also decides the composition**, as it did for the fusions in `03_`. It is
723 of the 876 nt and is GC3 96.7%, so it pulls the whole construct to a GC3 the
bare-tag versions never approach. The Waldo linker pulls very slightly the other
way (GC3 41.7% over 12 codons) but cannot offset it. Section 6 reports both.

**The Waldo linker ends in an in-frame EcoRI site.** `GAATTC` encodes Glu-Phe at
the linker's C terminus, which is how the folding-reporter constructs are built,
but it means the assembled ORF carries an internal EcoRI site. Section 1 counts
`GAATTC` occurrences per construct so that is visible before anyone picks cloning
enzymes.

**Two design consequences follow from the parts.** They are stated here because
the length numbers alone hide them:

- **No assembled ORF here has a terminal stop codon.** All the parts are
  stop-free, which is the correct basis for these metrics - every gene CDS here
  is stop-stripped too. But each plasmid needs a stop appended after the final
  part, and that is 3 nt this notebook does not count. Section 3 asserts the
  absence rather than leaving it implicit.
- **P2A separates the two halves, so the tag is on the downstream product, not on
  SmBiT.** 2A skipping happens between the final Gly and Pro of P2A, so every
  construct here makes the same 30-aa upstream product (SmBiT + 18 aa of P2A
  remnant) and a downstream product that differs: 10 aa for HA, 9 for FLAG, and
  **250 aa (~27.5 kDa) for FLAG-link-eGFP**. That last one is the only one of the
  three with enough mass to resolve on a gel - the bare FLAG and HA peptides work
  as a concept for "the second cistron was translated" but not as western
  targets. Section 3 reports every product so the choice is explicit.

# Load Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
```

```{r params}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05
cat("lfc_cutoff =", lfc_cutoff, "| padj_cutoff =", padj_cutoff, "\n")
```

# 1. Import and Verify the Parts

```{r read_parts}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

parts_tbl <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(parts_tbl)[1] <- "construct"

parts <- parts_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
stopifnot("Duplicate part names in cds seq.xlsx" = !any(duplicated(parts$part)))
pseq <- setNames(parts$seq, parts$part)

needed <- c("smbit n", "p2a", "ha", "flag3x", "egfp", "waldo linker", "nanoluc")
stopifnot(
  "A required part is missing from cds seq.xlsx" = all(needed %in% names(pseq)),
  "A part contains non-ACGT characters" = all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", pseq[needed])),
  "A part is not divisible by 3" = all(nchar(pseq[needed]) %% 3 == 0)
)

smbit_n <- pseq[["smbit n"]]
p2a     <- pseq[["p2a"]]
ha      <- pseq[["ha"]]
flag3x  <- pseq[["flag3x"]]
egfp    <- pseq[["egfp"]]
waldo   <- pseq[["waldo linker"]]

cat("Parts read from the spreadsheet:\n")
for (p in c("smbit n", "p2a", "ha", "flag3x", "waldo linker", "egfp")) {
  s <- pseq[[p]]
  cat(sprintf("  %-10s %3d nt (%3d codons)  %s\n", p, nchar(s), nchar(s) %/% 3,
              if (nchar(s) <= 90) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))
              else paste0(substr(as.character(translate(DNAString(s))), 1, 30),
                          "...")))
}
```

The 1x FLAG tag is cut from the C-terminal `DYKDDDDK` repeat of the supplied
`flag3x`, the same boundary `04_` and `05_` use, so the codons come from the
spreadsheet rather than being written here. No `ATG` is prepended to any tag:
unlike the FLAG fusions in `04_`, these tags sit downstream of P2A, not at the N
terminus.

```{r build_flag1x}
FLAG3X_AA <- "DYKDHDGDYKDHDIDYKDDDDK"
flag1x    <- substr(flag3x, 43, 66)

stopifnot(
  "flag3x does not encode the canonical 3xFLAG peptide" =
    as.character(translate(DNAString(flag3x))) == FLAG3X_AA,
  "1xFLAG is not 24 nt" = nchar(flag1x) == 24,
  "1xFLAG is not the C-terminal repeat of flag3x" = endsWith(flag3x, flag1x)
)
cat("1xFLAG cut from flag3x [43:66]:", flag1x, "\n")
```

eGFP is used exactly as supplied: 723 nt, its own `ATG` start, no stop codon. The
initiator is **kept**, so the FLAG-link-eGFP protein reads `...DYKDDDDK-M-VSKGEE...`
with a Met between tag and fluorophore. That is the ordinary N-terminal tagging
arrangement and costs one residue; `03_` uses the same eGFP sequence unchanged.

```{r verify_egfp}
EGFP_AA <- as.character(translate(DNAString(egfp)))
stopifnot(
  "egfp is not 723 nt"            = nchar(egfp) == 723,
  "egfp does not start with ATG"  = substr(egfp, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  "egfp carries a stop codon"     = !any(codon_split(egfp) %in% STOP_CODONS),
  # Biological spot-check: the GFP chromophore. avGFP numbers it T65-Y66-G67,
  # but eGFP carries an extra Val at position 2, so it sits at 66-68 here. The
  # position matters: TYG also occurs at residue 39, so asserting the motif is
  # merely present would pass on a sequence with no chromophore in place.
  "egfp protein does not carry the TYG chromophore at residues 66-68" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 66, 68) == "TYG",
  "egfp chromophore is not in the expected LTYGVQCF context" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 65, 72) == "LTYGVQCF",
  "egfp protein does not start with MVSKGEELFTG" =
    startsWith(EGFP_AA, "MVSKGEELFTG")
)
cat("eGFP:", nchar(egfp), "nt,", nchar(EGFP_AA), "aa, chromophore TYG at 66-68\n")
```

The Waldo folding-reporter linker joins the FLAG tag to eGFP. It ends in an
in-frame `GAATTC` EcoRI site, which is how these constructs are built but leaves
an internal EcoRI site in the ORF - counted below rather than discovered later.

```{r verify_waldo}
WALDO_AA <- "GSAGSAAGSGEF"
stopifnot(
  "waldo linker is not 36 nt"  = nchar(waldo) == 36,
  "waldo linker is not in frame" = nchar(waldo) %% 3 == 0,
  "waldo linker does not encode GSAGSAAGSGEF" =
    as.character(translate(DNAString(waldo))) == WALDO_AA,
  "waldo linker carries a stop codon" =
    !any(codon_split(waldo) %in% STOP_CODONS),
  # The EcoRI site must be in frame at the linker's 3' end, or the Glu-Phe it
  # encodes would not be the two residues the design expects.
  "waldo linker does not end with an in-frame GAATTC EcoRI site" =
    endsWith(waldo, "GAATTC") && (nchar(waldo) - 6) %% 3 == 0
)
cat("Waldo linker:", nchar(waldo), "nt,", WALDO_AA,
    "| GC3", round(compute_gc3_pct(waldo), 1), "%\n")
cat("Ends in an in-frame EcoRI site (GAATTC -> EF)\n")
```

The expected peptides are asserted, and in each case the reverse complement is
asserted **not** to encode them. A tag sequence can be in frame, the right
length, and still be backwards - that happened to the `flag3x` row - so an
orientation check that only confirmed the forward reading would pass either way
and tell us nothing.

```{r verify_peptides}
SMBIT_AA <- "VTGYRLFEEIL"   # NanoBiT small fragment, 11 aa
P2A_AA   <- "ATNFSLLKQAGDVEENPGP"
HA_AA    <- "YPYDVPDYA"
FLAG_AA  <- "DYKDDDDK"

aa_of <- function(s) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))
rc_aa <- function(s) as.character(translate(reverseComplement(DNAString(s))))

stopifnot(
  "smBit n does not start with ATG" = substr(smbit_n, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  "smBit n does not encode Met + the SmBiT peptide" =
    aa_of(smbit_n) == paste0("M", SMBIT_AA),
  "p2a does not encode the expected 19-aa P2A peptide" = aa_of(p2a) == P2A_AA,
  "HA does not encode the YPYDVPDYA epitope"           = aa_of(ha)  == HA_AA,
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope"        = aa_of(flag1x) == FLAG_AA
)
cat("Peptides confirmed: M+SmBiT, P2A, HA, 1xFLAG, eGFP\n")

stopifnot(
  "Both orientations encode SmBiT: the orientation check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(smbit_n) != paste0("M", SMBIT_AA),
  "Both orientations encode P2A: the orientation check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(p2a) != P2A_AA,
  "Both orientations encode HA: the orientation check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(ha) != HA_AA,
  "Both orientations encode FLAG: the orientation check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(flag1x) != FLAG_AA,
  "Both orientations encode eGFP: the orientation check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(egfp) != EGFP_AA
)
cat("No reverse complement encodes its own peptide, so the checks discriminate\n")

# No part may carry a stop codon, or the assembled ORF would terminate partway
# through.
stopifnot("A part carries a stop codon" =
            !any(map_lgl(list(smbit_n, p2a, ha, flag1x, egfp),
                         ~ any(codon_split(.x) %in% STOP_CODONS))))
cat("No part carries a stop codon\n")
```

# 2. SmBiT vs the NanoLuc C-terminus

SmBiT is derived from NanoLuc's C-terminal beta strand, so the two sequences are
similar but **not** identical, and the difference is the whole point of the
NanoBiT split. Pinning the relationship numerically means a change to either row
of the spreadsheet fires this check instead of the two drifting apart silently.

```{r smbit_vs_nanoluc}
nl <- load_nanoluc_construct()
nl_core_aa <- aa_of(nl$core)

# The aligned window: NanoLuc's catalytic ORF ends ...VTGWRLCERILA, so the 11-mer
# that lines up against SmBiT is the one ending one residue before the C terminus.
nl_window <- substr(nl_core_aa, nchar(nl_core_aa) - 11, nchar(nl_core_aa) - 1)
stopifnot("NanoLuc window is not 11 aa" = nchar(nl_window) == nchar(SMBIT_AA))

mism <- which(strsplit(nl_window, "")[[1]] != strsplit(SMBIT_AA, "")[[1]])
cat("NanoLuc C-terminal window:", nl_window, "\n")
cat("SmBiT                    :", SMBIT_AA, "\n")
cat("Mismatches:", length(mism), "at positions", paste(mism, collapse = ", "),
    sprintf("(%s)\n", paste(
      sprintf("%s%d%s",
              substring(nl_window, mism, mism), mism,
              substring(SMBIT_AA, mism, mism)), collapse = " ")))

stopifnot(
  # If this became 0, SmBiT would be the plain NanoLuc C-terminus and the split
  # reporter would not be a split reporter.
  "SmBiT is identical to the NanoLuc C-terminal window" = length(mism) > 0,
  "SmBiT differs from the NanoLuc C-terminal window by other than 3 residues" =
    length(mism) == 3,
  "SmBiT peptide is a substring of the NanoLuc protein" =
    !str_detect(nl_core_aa, fixed(SMBIT_AA))
)

# The codons differ too, not just the residues, so SmBiT was not cut out of this
# NanoLuc sequence.
cat("SmBiT DNA present in the NanoLuc construct:",
    str_detect(nl$full, fixed(substr(smbit_n, 4, nchar(smbit_n)))), "\n")
```

# 3. Assemble the Constructs

```{r assemble}
# Everything downstream of P2A, per construct. The Waldo linker sits between the
# FLAG tag and eGFP; eGFP keeps its own ATG.
tags <- list("HA"             = ha,
             "FLAG"           = flag1x,
             "FLAG-link-eGFP" = paste0(flag1x, waldo, egfp))
tag_aa <- list("HA"             = HA_AA,
               "FLAG"           = FLAG_AA,
               "FLAG-link-eGFP" = paste0(FLAG_AA, WALDO_AA, EGFP_AA))

stopifnot(
  "FLAG-link-eGFP tag is not FLAG + linker + eGFP" =
    tags[["FLAG-link-eGFP"]] == paste0(flag1x, waldo, egfp),
  "FLAG-link-eGFP tag length is not 24 + 36 + 723" =
    nchar(tags[["FLAG-link-eGFP"]]) ==
      nchar(flag1x) + nchar(waldo) + nchar(egfp),
  # The order matters and is asserted on the peptide: FLAG, then the linker,
  # then eGFP's initiator Met. Concatenating in the wrong order would still give
  # the right length and the right GC, so length alone cannot catch it.
  "FLAG-link-eGFP peptide does not read DYKDDDDK then the linker then Met" =
    str_detect(tag_aa[["FLAG-link-eGFP"]],
               fixed(paste0(FLAG_AA, WALDO_AA, "MVSKGEE")))
)

constructs <- map(tags, ~ paste0(smbit_n, p2a, .x))
names(constructs) <- paste0("SmBiT-P2A-", names(tags))

cat("Assembled ORF validation:\n")
iwalk(constructs, ~ check_orf(.x, .y))

iwalk(constructs, function(cs, nm) {
  tag_key <- sub("^SmBiT-P2A-", "", nm)
  tg      <- tags[[tag_key]]
  aa      <- aa_of(cs)
  stopifnot(
    "Construct length is not the sum of its parts" =
      nchar(cs) == nchar(smbit_n) + nchar(p2a) + nchar(tg),
    "Construct does not begin with the SmBiT part" = startsWith(cs, smbit_n),
    "Construct does not end with its tag part"     = endsWith(cs, tg),
    "P2A part is not bit-identical inside the construct" =
      substr(cs, nchar(smbit_n) + 1, nchar(smbit_n) + nchar(p2a)) == p2a,
    "P2A peptide not found exactly once in the construct protein" =
      lengths(gregexpr(P2A_AA, aa, fixed = TRUE)) == 1,
    # A frame slip at either join changes every downstream residue, so asserting
    # the protein ends in the tag peptide is what catches it.
    "Construct protein does not end with its tag peptide" =
      endsWith(aa, tag_aa[[tag_key]]),
    "Construct protein does not start with Met + SmBiT" =
      startsWith(aa, paste0("M", SMBIT_AA))
  )
})
cat("All", length(constructs),
    "constructs: length additive, single in-frame P2A, tag at the C terminus\n")

# Stated, not assumed: the assembled ORFs are stop-free, which matches the
# stop-stripped gene CDS basis but means each plasmid still needs a stop.
iwalk(constructs, function(cs, nm) {
  lc <- tail(codon_split(cs), 1)
  stopifnot("Assembled construct unexpectedly carries a terminal stop" =
              !lc %in% STOP_CODONS)
  cat(sprintf("  %-22s terminal codon %s (%s) - no stop; add one in the plasmid\n",
              nm, lc, substring(aa_of(cs), nchar(aa_of(cs)))))
})

# The constructs share the SmBiT + P2A head, so every length difference between
# them must be exactly the tag length difference.
head_nt <- nchar(smbit_n) + nchar(p2a)
stopifnot("A construct's length is not its tag length plus the shared head" =
            all(map_int(constructs, nchar) ==
                  head_nt + map_int(tags[sub("^SmBiT-P2A-", "",
                                             names(constructs))], nchar)))
cat("Shared SmBiT+P2A head:", head_nt, "nt; constructs differ only by the tag\n")

for (nm in names(constructs)) {
  cat("\n", nm, " (", nchar(constructs[[nm]]), " nt / ",
      nchar(aa_of(constructs[[nm]])), " aa )\n", sep = "")
}
```

P2A skipping happens between the final Gly and Pro of the P2A peptide, so the
ribosome makes two products from each ORF. Reporting both is the only way the
tag's position is explicit.

```{r p2a_products}
prod_tbl <- imap_dfr(constructs, function(cs, nm) {
  aa      <- aa_of(cs)
  tag_key <- sub("^SmBiT-P2A-", "", nm)
  skip_at <- str_locate(aa, fixed(P2A_AA))[1, "start"] + nchar(P2A_AA) - 2

  upstream   <- substr(aa, 1, skip_at)
  downstream <- substr(aa, skip_at + 1, nchar(aa))

  stopifnot(
    "P2A product split does not reconstitute the protein" =
      paste0(upstream, downstream) == aa,
    "Upstream product does not end at the P2A Gly-Pro junction" =
      endsWith(upstream, "EENPG"),
    "Downstream product is not Pro + the tag peptide" =
      downstream == paste0("P", tag_aa[[tag_key]])
  )

  tibble(construct = nm,
         product   = c("upstream (SmBiT + P2A remnant)",
                       paste0("downstream (Pro + ", tag_key, ")")),
         aa        = c(nchar(upstream), nchar(downstream)),
         approx_kda = round(c(nchar(upstream), nchar(downstream)) * 0.11, 1))
})
print(prod_tbl)

# The upstream product is identical for all three constructs: the tag is entirely
# downstream of the skip, so it cannot affect the SmBiT half.
up <- prod_tbl %>% filter(str_starts(product, "upstream"))
stopifnot("Upstream products differ between constructs" = n_distinct(up$aa) == 1)
cat("\nAll constructs make the identical", up$aa[1],
    "aa upstream product; the tag is only on the downstream peptide.\n")

# Only the eGFP construct's downstream product has enough mass to run on a gel.
big <- prod_tbl %>% filter(str_starts(product, "downstream"), aa >= 50)
cat("Downstream products large enough to resolve on a gel (>= 50 aa):",
    if (nrow(big)) paste(big$construct, collapse = ", ") else "none", "\n")
```

```{r construct_table}
ref_df <- tibble(
  reporter   = names(constructs),
  cds_length = map_int(constructs, nchar),
  gc_pct     = map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc_pct),
  gc3_pct    = map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc3_pct)
)

stopifnot(
  "Reporter GC% out of range"  = all(ref_df$gc_pct  >= 0 & ref_df$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "Reporter GC3% out of range" = all(ref_df$gc3_pct >= 0 & ref_df$gc3_pct <= 100)
)
print(ref_df %>% mutate(across(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), ~ round(.x, 1))))

# Okabe-Ito dark blue / bluish green / reddish purple: avoid the density-curve
# hues (grey70 / #E69F00) and the two reserved factor hues (#E69F00 eIF3d,
# #56B4E9 eIF3e).
ref_plot_df <- ref_df %>%
  mutate(color    = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7")[
           match(reporter, names(constructs))],
         linetype = "solid")
```

# 4. MDA-MB-231 Background and Gene Set

```{r load_promotes}
te_hyp <- read_csv(
  here("output", "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_hypoxia_1hr.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Direction check. These files hold the sictrl_vs_si3d coefficient despite the
# filename stating the ratio the other way round, so positive te_lfc = eIF3d
# promotes. EIF3D's own rna_lfc must be strongly positive because the siRNA
# depletes its target.
eif3d_rna <- te_hyp %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D") %>% pull(rna_lfc)
stopifnot("EIF3D rna_lfc is not strongly positive: contrast direction may be flipped" =
            length(eif3d_rna) == 1 && eif3d_rna > 2)
cat("Direction check - EIF3D rna_lfc:", round(eif3d_rna, 2), "\n")

promotes <- te_hyp %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))
stopifnot("Expected 1604 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes" = nrow(promotes) == 1604)
cat("eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes:", nrow(promotes), "\n")
```

```{r transcripts}
fm <- readRDS(here("output", "predictive_modeling",
                   "feature_matrix_external_stability.rds"))
tx_all      <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)
tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

missing_gene_ids <- promotes$gene_id_clean[
  !promotes$gene_id_clean %in% tx_all$gene_id_clean]

tx_map <- read_tsv(
  here("accessories", "human", "tx2gene_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv.gz"),
  col_names = c("transcript_id", "gene_id"), col_types = "cc") %>%
  filter(str_starts(transcript_id, "ENST")) %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", transcript_id),
            gene_id_clean       = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

hyp_samples <- c("NM2025_0094", "NM2025_0095", "NM2025_0096")
hyp_files   <- setNames(
  file.path(here("2025_MDAcells_riboseq", "salmon"), hyp_samples, "quant.sf.gz"),
  hyp_samples)
stopifnot("Hypoxia siCTRL quant files missing" = all(file.exists(hyp_files)))

extra_tx_df <- map_dfr(names(hyp_files), function(s) {
  read_tsv(hyp_files[[s]], col_types = "cdddd",
           col_names = c("Name", "Length", "EffectiveLength", "TPM", "NumReads"),
           skip = 1) %>% dplyr::select(Name, TPM)
}) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% summarise(mean_tpm = mean(TPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", Name)) %>%
  inner_join(tx_map, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(gene_id_clean %in% missing_gene_ids, mean_tpm > 0) %>%
  group_by(gene_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_tpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(promotes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol) %>% distinct(),
            by = "gene_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

tx_promotes <- bind_rows(tx_promotes, extra_tx_df)
cat("Promoted genes with a transcript:", nrow(tx_promotes), "\n")
```

```{r build_metrics}
metrics_all <- build_cds_metrics(
  here("accessories", "human", "txdb.gencode49.sqlite"))

expressed <- tx_all %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)
promoted <- tx_promotes %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)

cat("Expressed transcriptome - valid CDS:", nrow(expressed), "\n")
cat("eIF3d promoted        - valid CDS:", nrow(promoted), "\n")

stopifnot(
  "GC% out of range"  = all(expressed$gc_pct  >= 0 & expressed$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "GC3% out of range" = all(expressed$gc3_pct >= 0 & expressed$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "GC3 median not in expected range [40, 65]" =
    between(median(expressed$gc3_pct), 40, 65)
)

actb <- expressed %>% filter(symbol == "ACTB") %>% dplyr::slice(1)
if (nrow(actb) == 1) {
  stopifnot("ACTB CDS GC% outside expected 50-70%" = between(actb$gc_pct, 50, 70))
  cat("ACTB CDS GC%:", round(actb$gc_pct, 2),
      "| GC3%:", round(actb$gc3_pct, 2), "\n")
}

cat(sprintf("\nShortest expressed CDS: %s nt\n", fmt_n(min(expressed$cds_length))))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ref_df))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-22s %4d nt | expressed shorter: %s of %s\n",
              ref_df$reporter[i], ref_df$cds_length[i],
              fmt_n(sum(expressed$cds_length < ref_df$cds_length[i])),
              fmt_n(nrow(expressed))))
}
```

# 5. Density Panels

Every legend entry carries the number it stands for: each density curve shows its
group median, each reference line its own value. Units follow the metric, not the
axis - the length axis is drawn in kb because kb ticks are readable, but a
construct is specified in nt, so the labels say nt.

```{r density_setup}
group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")

# NanoLuc is deliberately not a reference line here. Asserted rather than
# assumed, so re-adding it to ref_plot_df without updating the prose fires.
stopifnot(
  "NanoLuc should not be among the plotted reference lines" =
    !any(str_detect(tolower(ref_plot_df$reporter), "nanoluc|nluc")),
  "Expected exactly three reference lines" = nrow(ref_plot_df) == 3
)

# Three cumulative views. Keeping the earlier ones means a figure made from this
# notebook before the eGFP construct existed can still be regenerated.
views <- list(
  list(key = "smbit_p2a_ha",
       reporters = "SmBiT-P2A-HA",
       title = "SmBiT-P2A-HA"),
  list(key = "smbit_p2a_ha_flag",
       reporters = c("SmBiT-P2A-HA", "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG"),
       title = "SmBiT-P2A-HA and -FLAG"),
  # Named generically rather than listing all three: spelling them out overruns
  # the plot width at 9.5 in and the title is clipped. The legend names them.
  list(key = "smbit_p2a_all",
       reporters = c("SmBiT-P2A-HA", "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG", "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"),
       title = "SmBiT-P2A constructs")
)
stopifnot("A view names a reporter that does not exist" =
            all(unlist(map(views, "reporters")) %in% ref_plot_df$reporter))
```

```{r panels, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5, results='hold'}
for (v in views) {
  rp <- ref_plot_df %>% filter(reporter %in% v$reporters)
  stopifnot("View selected the wrong number of reference lines" =
              nrow(rp) == length(v$reporters))

  plot_density_luc(
    expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
    xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
    title   = paste0("CDS length, MDA-MB-231, ", v$title),
    outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_06_density_cds_length_", v$key, ".pdf"),
    luc_tbl = rp, group_cols = group_cols, xscale = 1000, xmax = 6)

  # The bare-tag constructs land at ~0.12 kb, 2% of the way across the panel
  # above, where they sit on the axis. The zoom is the readable version; the
  # densities are unchanged, only the visible range differs.
  plot_density_luc(
    expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
    xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
    # Same title as the wide panel: the zoom is a view of the same data, and the
    # axis shows the range. The filename carries the distinction.
    title   = paste0("CDS length, MDA-MB-231, ", v$title),
    outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_06_density_cds_length_", v$key,
                     "_zoom2kb.pdf"),
    luc_tbl = rp, group_cols = group_cols, xscale = 1000, xmax = 2)

  plot_density_luc(
    expressed, promoted, "gc_pct",
    xlab    = "CDS GC content (%)",
    title   = paste0("CDS GC content, MDA-MB-231, ", v$title),
    outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_06_density_cds_gc_", v$key, ".pdf"),
    luc_tbl = rp, group_cols = group_cols)

  plot_density_luc(
    expressed, promoted, "gc3_pct",
    xlab    = "CDS GC3 content (%)",
    title   = paste0("CDS GC3 content, MDA-MB-231, ", v$title),
    outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_06_density_cds_gc3_", v$key, ".pdf"),
    luc_tbl = rp, group_cols = group_cols)
}
```

# 6. Percentiles, Part Contributions and How Little the Bare Tags Separate

```{r percentiles}
pct_tbl <- reporter_percentiles(expressed, promoted, ref_df)
print(pct_tbl)

stopifnot("Percentiles must lie in [0, 100]" =
            all(pct_tbl$pct_expressed >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_expressed <= 100 &
                pct_tbl$pct_promoted  >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_promoted  <= 100))

write_csv(pct_tbl,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design", "06_smbit_percentiles_vs_231.csv"))
cat("Exported: output/cds_reporter_design/06_smbit_percentiles_vs_231.csv\n")
```

The two bare-tag constructs are one point for this analysis; FLAG-link-eGFP is not.
Quantifying both spreads is the honest version of what the overlapping reference
lines show.

```{r spread}
spread_of <- function(d, label) {
  tibble(
    set    = label,
    metric = c("cds_length", "gc_pct", "gc3_pct"),
    min    = c(min(d$cds_length), min(d$gc_pct), min(d$gc3_pct)),
    max    = c(max(d$cds_length), max(d$gc_pct), max(d$gc3_pct))
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      construct_range = max - min,
      # How much of each gene distribution's own spread that range covers. A tiny
      # fraction means the constructs are, for this analysis, one point.
      gene_iqr_expressed = c(IQR(expressed$cds_length), IQR(expressed$gc_pct),
                             IQR(expressed$gc3_pct)),
      pct_of_gene_iqr = round(100 * construct_range / gene_iqr_expressed, 1),
      across(c(min, max, construct_range, gene_iqr_expressed), ~ round(.x, 1))
    )
}

spread <- bind_rows(
  spread_of(ref_df %>% filter(reporter != "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"), "bare tags"),
  spread_of(ref_df, "all three")
)
print(spread)

# Discriminative: adding eGFP must widen the length spread by far more than the
# bare pair's own range, or the two sets would not be worth reporting apart.
bare_len <- spread$construct_range[spread$set == "bare tags" &
                                     spread$metric == "cds_length"]
all_len  <- spread$construct_range[spread$set == "all three" &
                                     spread$metric == "cds_length"]
stopifnot("Adding eGFP did not widen the length spread" = all_len > 10 * bare_len)

write_csv(spread,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design", "06_smbit_construct_spread.csv"))
```

```{r part_contributions}
part_df <- tibble(
  part = c("SmBiT (ATG + 11 aa)", "P2A", "HA (1x)", "FLAG (1x)",
           "Waldo linker", "eGFP", names(constructs)),
  seq  = c(smbit_n, p2a, ha, flag1x, waldo, egfp,
           unlist(constructs, use.names = FALSE))
) %>%
  transmute(part,
            nt      = nchar(seq),
            codons  = nchar(seq) %/% 3,
            gc_pct  = map_dbl(seq, gc_pct_of),
            gc3_pct = map_dbl(seq, compute_gc3_pct)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), ~ round(.x, 1)))
print(part_df)

getnt <- function(p) part_df$nt[part_df$part == p]
stopifnot(
  "HA part table does not sum to the construct length" =
    getnt("SmBiT (ATG + 11 aa)") + getnt("P2A") + getnt("HA (1x)") ==
      getnt("SmBiT-P2A-HA"),
  "FLAG part table does not sum to the construct length" =
    getnt("SmBiT (ATG + 11 aa)") + getnt("P2A") + getnt("FLAG (1x)") ==
      getnt("SmBiT-P2A-FLAG"),
  "FLAG-link-eGFP part table does not sum to the construct length" =
    getnt("SmBiT (ATG + 11 aa)") + getnt("P2A") + getnt("FLAG (1x)") +
      getnt("Waldo linker") + getnt("eGFP") ==
        getnt("SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP")
)

# Internal EcoRI sites, which the Waldo linker introduces by design. Reported
# rather than asserted away: it is a property of the linker, not a defect, but
# it has to be visible before anyone picks cloning enzymes.
ecori <- tibble(
  construct = names(constructs),
  n_ecori   = map_int(constructs, ~ str_count(.x, fixed("GAATTC")))
)
print(ecori)
stopifnot(
  "The linker-bearing construct should carry exactly one EcoRI site" =
    ecori$n_ecori[ecori$construct == "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"] == 1,
  # Discriminative: the bare-tag constructs have no linker, so they must have
  # no EcoRI site, or the count is picking up something other than the linker.
  "A construct without the linker carries an EcoRI site" =
    all(ecori$n_ecori[ecori$construct != "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"] == 0)
)

write_csv(part_df,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design", "06_smbit_part_composition.csv"))

# eGFP's share of the eGFP construct, which is why that construct's composition
# is eGFP's composition.
egfp_share <- 100 * nchar(egfp) / nchar(constructs[["SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"]])
cat(sprintf("\neGFP is %.1f%% of SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP by length, at GC3 %.1f%%;\n",
            egfp_share, compute_gc3_pct(egfp)))
cat(sprintf("the assembled construct lands at GC3 %.1f%% against a transcriptome median of %.1f%%\n",
            ref_df$gc3_pct[ref_df$reporter == "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-eGFP"],
            median(expressed$gc3_pct)))

seq_out <- tibble(
  reporter = names(constructs),
  length_nt_stop_free = map_int(constructs, nchar),
  gc_pct   = round(map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc_pct), 3),
  gc3_pct  = round(map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc3_pct), 3),
  protein  = map_chr(constructs, aa_of),
  bases    = unlist(constructs, use.names = FALSE)
)
write_csv(seq_out,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               "06_smbit_assembled_sequences.csv"))
cat("Exported: 06_smbit_part_composition.csv, 06_smbit_construct_spread.csv,",
    "06_smbit_assembled_sequences.csv\n")
```

cat("=== SmBiT-P2A-tag constructs vs MDA-MB-231 ===\n\n")

cat("eGFP is used as supplied, keeping its own ATG. No ATG on the tags: they\n")

cat(sprintf("                    promoted      %.0f nt / GC %.1f%% / GC3 %.1f%%\n",

            median(promoted$gc3_pct)))

}

}

cat("\nP2A products:\n")
